stages.title: What Graphic Design Is For
stages.description: Graphic design as visual communication: ordering a message so a specific group can receive it, with type and image doing work that words alone do not.
learningObjectives: Define graphic design as a profession and an applied art
Explain the designer's role in encoding a message
Distinguish giving order to information from advertising's aim to sell
Name a few of the objects the profession actually produces

explainBack.question: Someone asks you to 'make a logo and a poster.' Explain what graphic design is doing in that job, how it differs from advertising's purpose, and why type and image are part of the message.
rubric: Graphic design creates visual communications meant to carry a specific message to a specific group
The designer interprets, orders and presents that message; a linguistic brief becomes a graphic form
Typography and the arrangement of text, ornament and image convey ideas beyond language alone
Advertising's objective is the sale; graphic design's essence is to give order to information and form to ideas
The work includes logos, packaging, posters, signage, editorial pages and websites, not only sketches

resources.title: Graphic design
resources.description: Encyclopedia overview of graphic design as visual communication, its history in print, and what the profession produces.
keyPoints: Graphic design creates visual communications that transmit a specific message to a social group
The designer encodes the message: interpretation, ordering and presentation
Type, ornament and image convey ideas beyond what language alone expresses
Meggs's formulation: the essence is to give order to information and form to ideas, which is distinct from advertising's aim to sell
The term appears in print by 1908, and a Graphic Design and Lettering course was advertised in 1917

resources.title: Figma For Beginners: Create designs (2/4)
resources.description: Figma's beginner lesson on turning a wireframe into a design, including color, type, images and alignment.
keyPoints: The same layer tools used for wireframes carry into a higher-fidelity design
Color and typography are introduced alongside precision and accessibility
Place Image, or the shortcut, fills a shape with a picture
There is more than one path from a blank frame to a finished design

resources.title: Ultimate Guide to Typography in Design
resources.description: How alignment and a clear size order help a reader move through a poster, a screen or an infographic.
keyPoints: Aligning a logo, image, heading and body to one edge makes the path down the page easier to follow
Headings should be larger than subheadings, and subheadings larger than body text
Website body text is typically 16px, with an H1 often around 48px
A typeface should match the tone: a plain sans for a professional voice, a decorative face used sparingly

stages.title: Type Size, Measure and Line Height
stages.description: Choosing a typeface on purpose, then setting how long a line is and how much air sits between lines.
learningObjectives: Separate a typeface from a font
Give a useful range for line length
Explain why line height should open up as the line gets longer
Start a type system from body text rather than from the display size

explainBack.question: You are setting a paragraph on a phone and the same paragraph on a wide desktop. Explain how you would choose the type, how long each line should be, and how line height should change.
rubric: A typeface is what you see; a font is the file you use
Bringhurst's satisfactory line is about 45 to 75 characters for a single column of serif text; Material Design suggests about 40 to 60 on screen
As the measure gets wider, the line height should get more open so the eye can find the next line
A practical line height for Latin text often sits between 115% and 150% of the font size
Start with body text at the narrowest viewport, then adjust as the line length changes

resources.title: Fonts Knowledge
resources.description: Google Fonts' library of guides for choosing and using type, including the glossary that separates a typeface from a font.
keyPoints: The guides are for choosing and using type with a purpose, not only picking a favourite from a menu
A typeface is what you see; a font is what you use
X-height is the height of lowercase letters without ascenders or descenders, and it changes how large the type looks
Readability, legibility and accessibility are treated as the point of setting type

resources.title: Understanding measure and line length
resources.description: Why a line that is too long or too short is hard to read, with Bringhurst's and Material Design's ranges.
keyPoints: Measure is line length, and flexible web layouts made overly long lines common
Bringhurst calls 45 to 75 characters a satisfactory line for a single column of serif text
Material Design suggests about 40 to 60 characters for body text on screen
As the measure grows wider, the leading should grow too

resources.title: Choosing a suitable line height
resources.description: How line height relates to font size and to the length of the line.
keyPoints: A line height of 150% multiplies the font size by 1.5
For Latin text, a useful range is often 115% to 150%
Languages with many diacritics usually need more leading
Wider measures need more open line height
Start from body text at the narrowest screen, then adjust

resources.title: Kick-start your typography system in Figma
resources.description: How a small set of sizes and line heights, often on an 8-point grid, stays usable across screens.
keyPoints: A type system needs enough sizes for display and body text, and not so many that nobody knows which to use
Decorative faces can be reserved for large text; a legible face carries the body copy
An 8-point grid spaces and sizes elements in multiples of 8, often with a 4-point baseline for type
Line heights in multiples of 4 keep vertical rhythm and alignment across columns

stages.title: Color for Screens and for Print
stages.description: Why screen color is light and print color is ink, and why text contrast is a light-dark ratio rather than a hue.
learningObjectives: Contrast RGB with CMYK
Explain why black ink is added to cyan, magenta and yellow
State the WCAG minimum contrast for body text and for large text
Say which text is exempt from that ratio

explainBack.question: A poster will be printed, and the same words will also sit on a website. Explain which color model each uses, and what contrast the body text and the large title each need on screen.
rubric: RGB is additive: colors are emitted light, white is all primaries together, and black is the absence of light
CMYK is subtractive printing: cyan, magenta, yellow and black ink reduce light reflected from the paper
Black ink is the key plate; combining cyan, magenta and yellow alone makes a poor black and uses more ink
WCAG 2.1 requires at least 4.5:1 for ordinary text and 3:1 for large-scale text
Incidental text, decoration, and text that is part of a logo or brand name have no contrast requirement

resources.title: CMYK color model
resources.description: How four-color printing uses cyan, magenta, yellow and black, and how that differs from light on a screen.
keyPoints: CMYK is a subtractive model used in color printing
Inks reduce light reflected from a white background; white is the paper
RGB is additive: white is all primaries and black is no light
The K plate is black, used for sharper text and a more consistent dark than cyan, magenta and yellow alone
Halftoning varies dot size and spacing so a printer can suggest tones between the inks

resources.title: Understanding Success Criterion 1.4.3: Contrast (Minimum)
resources.description: The WCAG explanation of minimum text contrast, including large text, logos and decoration.
keyPoints: Ordinary text needs a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against its background
Large-scale text needs at least 3:1; 18 point, or 14 point bold, is the usual threshold
The ratio is about light and dark, not hue, so it still applies for many kinds of color vision deficiency
Inactive controls, pure decoration and text inside a logo have no contrast requirement
4.499:1 does not meet 4.5:1; the threshold is not rounded up

resources.title: Typography
resources.description: Material Design's notes on line length and on keeping text contrast high enough to read.
keyPoints: Text that is too close to the background is hard to read, and extreme contrast can be hard as well
Material asks for at least 4.5:1, and prefers 7:1
About 60 characters per line is a readable measure for body text
A line that is too long is hard to track; a line that is too short breaks the reading rhythm

stages.title: Layout Grids
stages.description: Using columns, rows and a baseline so type, images and spacing line up, including when the frame changes size.
learningObjectives: Say what a grid contributes to hierarchy and rhythm
Name Figma's three layout-grid forms
Describe a baseline grid and the 4-point interval used with an 8-point system
Explain how constraints behave differently once a layout grid is present

explainBack.question: You are laying out a poster in Figma that also has to become a phone screen. Explain what you would put a grid on, which kinds of grid you can stack, and how a baseline grid relates to the type.
rubric: A grid defines structure, hierarchy and rhythm and removes guesswork from position, size and spacing
In Figma a layout grid applies to a frame, and a frame can hold more than one grid
The three forms are a uniform grid, columns and rows
A baseline grid repeats vertically from the lines type sits on; an 8-point system often uses a 4-point baseline
With a layout grid, constraints pin an object to the nearest column rather than only to the frame edge

resources.title: Figma Tutorial: Layout Grids
resources.description: Figma's own lesson on adding column and row grids, gutters, margins and stretch, center or left behavior.
keyPoints: A frame can hold columns, rows, or both
Gutter is the space between columns or rows; margin is the space at the outer edge
Stretch makes a column grow and shrink with the frame; Center and Left allow a set width
Layout grids can be shown or hidden for the whole file

resources.title: Everything you need to know about layout grids in Figma
resources.description: How columns, rows, baseline grids and constraints keep a layout consistent from print habits to many screen sizes.
keyPoints: A suitable grid defines structure, hierarchy and rhythm
Layout grids apply only to frames, and one frame can hold several
The three forms are a uniform grid, columns and rows
Many 8-point systems use a 4-point baseline so type size and line height stay scalable
Constraints inside a layout grid relate to the nearest column, which keeps gutters stable when the frame resizes

stages.title: Vectors, Pixels and Type Outlines
stages.description: Why a logo wants geometry that can scale, and why a photograph does not.
learningObjectives: Define vector graphics against raster graphics
Name the basic geometric primitives
Explain why vectors suit logos and type, and rasters suit photographs
Describe a glyph outline as Bézier curves that are later rasterized

explainBack.question: A client wants a logo that will be printed on a pen and on a building, plus a photograph of the product. Explain which should be vector, which should be a bitmap, and what happens to a font outline on screen.
rubric: Vector images are built from geometric shapes such as points, lines, curves and polygons on a coordinate plane
A square, a line, or a curve can be stored as a few vertices; the software fills in the rest
Vectors are preferred where precision and scaling matter, including typography; photographs are a raster job
A digital glyph is drawn with Bézier curves, which keep their shape when scaled because they are coordinates
On screen those outlines are rasterized into pixels; hinting helps that grid at small sizes

resources.title: Vector graphics
resources.description: How vector images store geometry instead of a grid of pixels, and where that model fits or fails.
keyPoints: Vector graphics build images from points, lines, curves and polygons
They are an alternative to raster graphics, and each fits different jobs
Primitives include a point, a line segment, a polyline and a polygon, plus curves such as Bézier curves
Typography and logos want that precision; photography is a raster problem
Converting between vector formats can be lossless when both formats support the same primitives

resources.title: Outlines
resources.description: How a glyph is drawn with Bézier curves and then turned into pixels or print dots.
keyPoints: A glyph is the drawn shape of a character
Digital type usually draws those shapes as Bézier curves, which scale without losing the coordinates
What you see is a rendering: pixels on screen, dots in print
Contour direction tells the rasterizer what is filled and what is a counter
Hinting adds instructions so small sizes still look like the design

stages.title: Reusable Color and Text Styles
stages.description: Saving a fill and a text treatment once so a change updates every place that treatment is used.
learningObjectives: Explain what a style is separate from the object it is applied to
Create a color style from a fill
Say what a text style is for
Note that a style belongs to the file until it is published

explainBack.question: You have used the same gray and the same heading size in twenty frames. Explain how Figma styles let you change them once, and what is left behind if you delete one of the frames.
rubric: A style is a named set of properties that can be reused
A color style is created from a fill and then applied to objects; the object is not the style
Deleting the object does not delete the style, because the style belongs to the file
Text styles define a typographic scale and can be applied to a whole text layer
Using a style in another file requires publishing it as a library

resources.title: Figma Tutorial: Creating Styles
resources.description: Figma's lesson on saving a fill as a color style that lives in the file, not on the shape.
keyPoints: A repeated fill is worth saving as a color style so it can be reused
The style is created from the fill and given a name
The shape on the canvas uses the style; deleting the shape does not delete the style
Local styles belong to the file and can be edited or deleted from the style list

resources.title: Create and apply text styles
resources.description: Figma's help page on text styles as a reusable typographic scale.
keyPoints: A style is a set of properties reused across files and projects
Text styles define the typographic scale
A text style can apply to a whole layer
A style in the current file can be reused there; another file needs the style published as a library

stages.title: Sharing a Grid Across Frames
stages.description: Turning a column plan, a baseline and a padding guide into a style a team can apply again.
learningObjectives: Use a grid to visualize padding
Nest a grid inside a frame that already has a grid
Combine grids into one shared style
Say why the same grid idea still matters on screens of different sizes

explainBack.question: A desktop frame and a phone frame need the same margins and column logic. Explain how you would build that in Figma and hand the same grids to the rest of the team.
rubric: Grids still matter on screens because they keep a layout consistent across viewport sizes
A single-column and single-row grid with the gutter at 0 and a margin set to the spacing value can show padding
A grid can sit on a nested frame, so one area of a layout can have its own grid
Several grids can be saved as one grid style and shared from a team library

resources.title: Layout grids: padding, nesting and styles
resources.description: The same Figma article's later sections on padding guides, nested grids and publishing a grid style. Used here for those sections.
keyPoints: Print grid ideas still matter on screen, where the viewport changes
A one-column and one-row grid with zero gutter and a set margin visualizes padding
Nested frames can each carry their own grid
Several grids can be combined into one style and shared from a team library

stages.title: Who the Work Belongs To
stages.description: Copyright in an original artistic work, including a design, and what a copyright line does not add.
learningObjectives: State that UK copyright in an original artistic work is automatic
List uses that need permission
Explain the effect of adding ©
Note overseas protection in outline

explainBack.question: You design an original poster in the UK for a client, and you also keep a version in your portfolio. Explain what copyright exists in the artwork, what other people cannot do with it, and whether a © mark is what creates the right.
rubric: Original artistic work, including illustration, is protected automatically when it is created
There is no UK application, fee or register
Copying, distributing, showing the work in public, adapting it or putting it on the internet needs permission
Adding ©, a name and the year does not change the level of protection
Agreements such as the Berne Convention can protect the work in other countries

resources.title: How copyright protects your work
resources.description: The UK overview of automatic copyright, including original artistic work such as illustration.
keyPoints: Protection is automatic and there is no UK copyright register
Original artistic work, including illustration and photography, is covered
Others cannot copy, distribute, show, adapt or upload the work without permission
A © mark with a name and year does not change the strength of the right
The Berne Convention can extend protection abroad

name: Graphic Design
description: Learn to give a message a visual form: what graphic design is for, type size and line length, color for print and screens, layout grids, vectors, reusable styles, and the copyright in the work.
